# CANDIDATE: MIDDAY_VOL_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When intraday volatility contracts sharply over the lunch hour (12:00-13:00 ET), the subsequent breakout after 13:00 ET tends to capture the next directional move. This anomaly exists because liquidity consolidates during lunch, reducing noise and allowing clearer institutional order flow to drive price after 13:00. The strategy captures this by entering on the first 13:00 bar that breaks the lunch window's high/low with confirmation of volatility compression.

## Mechanism

At 13:00 ET, calculate ATR(5) and ATR(20) using the prior 20-period (i.e., ATR(5) of the last 5 bars, ATR(20) of the last 20 bars, both ending at 12:55 ET). If ATR(5) < 0.5 * ATR(20) (volatility compression) AND price closes above the high of the 12:00-13:00 window, go long; if price closes below the low of that window, go short. Exit: chart-stop at the opposite window extreme (i.e., for longs, stop at lunch window low; for shorts, stop at lunch window high), TP1 at 1.5R, runner using a chandelier trail (ATR*2). Regime filter: only trade on days with VIX 15-25 and morning price within VWAP ± 0.5*ATR (9:30-12:00 ET) to avoid strong trending mornings.

2. **Sample bias:** Idea derived from intraday volatility patterns observed in 2025-2026 SPY 5m data; sample size is all days in that period; overfit risk is high without walk-forward validation because the mechanism is based on a single time-of-day pattern that may not persist.
